rationale: PINS THE TWO RULED EXTENDED TYPES (`renders`, `mixes_in`) BESIDE THE CONSTRUCTS THAT MAKE THE RULING TRUE, so the ruling is a measurement and a control rather than an absence. THE RULING'S EVIDENCE (whole admitted population, 3,702 .hs/.lhs files over 6 repositories, validation/m14/measurements/haskell-extended-census.json): `renders` 0 sites — the nearest analogue (a Template Haskell template LOADER) is 0 sites and names a FILE, not a component symbol, so the vocabulary's component->component relation has nothing to bind; `mixes_in` has no construct — the served grammar's 174 distinct named types (253 named slots of 552 ids, digest 37a6b07b1a83) contain no mixin/trait/composition node, and the family a mixin would have to come from is CONFORMANCE, pinned here as `extends` (superclass constraint), `implements` (instance) and `overrides` (instance method). FORBID (A) is the load-bearing negative: `deriving (Semigroup, Monoid) via (Sum Int)` is the closest construct in the language to implementation composition — 493 corpus sites — and it is conformance obtained THROUGH a carrier, which attaches no member set and puts nothing in a supertype chain; the analyzer reads it as `implements` with metadata.derived, never as mixes_in. FORBID (B) is the renders negative: a function producing a markup String is a VALUE producer, not a component rendered by a host; a rule keyed on `String`-returning functions would emit it. FIRE rows are the same three conformance constructors the ruling leans on, so a lane that silenced them to 'clean up' the extended verdicts would fail this fixture.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: THE RULING, PINNED AS A COUNT. Haskell has no member-set composition: `deriving via` is conformance through a carrier, and the typeclass family is extends/implements/overrides above. A rule that relabelled the 493 deriving-via sites as mixes_in would fire the moment a fixture carried one — this one does.

THE SECOND RULING, PINNED AS A COUNT. This file contains a function that assembles a markup String, which is the only render-shaped thing an fp language can write. No host renderer constructs an element here, and the target would be a value, not a declaration.
EXACTLY the superclass constraint. An over-eager rule that read every `=>` as an inheritance edge (the corpus has 6,124 `=>` sites; 189 became edges) would add rows here.
